subsection.name: Prerequisites
subsection.p: Before starting, ensure you have the following installed:

ul.li: Web Browser (Chrome / Firefox / Edge to check compatibility)

subsection.name: Repository Setup and Initial Build

p.strong: Clone the HtmlUnit repository from GitHub:
Compile the project to ensure everything is working correctly:

subsection.p: Do not run the whole test suite as it takes a significant amount of time.

subsection.name: Eclipse IDE Setup
subsection.p: Use the Maven Eclipse Plugin to generate project files with source downloads:
Then import the project into Eclipse:

p.code: File → Import → Existing Projects into Workspace

subsection.p: Usually you would run only select tests from Eclipse. Refer to the section on real browser testing below for details.

subsection.name: IntelliJ IDEA Project Setup
subsection.p: IntelliJ IDEA has built-in Maven support and can directly import the HtmlUnit project.

ol.li: Navigate to the cloned HtmlUnit directory
Select the pom.xml file and click Open
Choose Open as Project when prompted
IntelliJ will automatically detect the Maven project and import it

subsection.name: Running Tests via Maven
subsection.p: Running the full test suite requires significant time and resources. Several profiles are defined to run distinct test sets:
Fast core test suite (~25 min; excludes library and heavy tests):
Runs test suites from various JavaScript libraries (jQuery, Prototype, etc.):
Tests assume port 12345 is available. If you encounter java.net.BindException: Address already in use, override the test port:

subsection.name: Running Tests with Real Browsers
subsection.p: The primary goal of HtmlUnit is providing accurate browser simulation. Almost all tests can be executed against real browsers using Selenium WebDriver.
This is managed via org.htmlunit.WebDriverTestCase. To configure real browser runs, create a test.properties file in the HtmlUnit root directory:
subsection.source:
browsers=hu #browsers=hu-ff #browsers=hu-ff, hu-chrome #browsers=ff, chrome, edge
# Unix/Linux paths ff.bin=/usr/bin/firefox ff-esr.bin=/usr/bin/firefox-esr geckodriver.bin=/usr/bin/driver/geckodriver chrome.bin=/path/to/chromedriver edge.bin=/path/to/chromedriver
# Windows paths geckodriver.bin=C:\\path\\to\\geckodriver.exe ff.bin=C:\\path\\to\\Mozilla Firefox\\firefox.exe ff-esr.bin=C:\\path\\to\\Mozilla Firefox ESR\\firefox.exe chrome.bin=C:\\path\\to\\chromedriver.exe edge.bin=C:\\path\\to\\msedgedriver.exe
# optional autofix=false
subsection.p: browsers: Comma-separated combination of target environments:

ul.li: ff, ff-esr, chrome, edge (Real browsers via WebDriver)
edge.bin: Path to Edge WebDriver binary
autofix: Automatically update expectations or @NotYetImplemented annotations.
